 Hon’ble  the  Chief  Justice  of  India  pronounced  the
Judgment f or himself and on behalf of S.V.N. Bhatti, Joymalya
Bagchi, N.V. Anjaria, Arun Palli and V. Mohana, JJ.
                   
         In light of the conclusions and findings recorded in the
signed reportable judgment, we deem it appropriate to direct as
follows:
i. The  reference  is  answered  as  having  been  rendered
infructuous. The question of the legislative competence of
the State Legislatures to levy the impugned surcharges
shall be governed by the law declared in S. Kodar;
ii. The questions as to (a) the validity of Section 30-AA of
the Punjab General Sales Tax Act, 1948, insofar as it
requires industrial units otherwise exempted from sales
tax to pay the surcharge; and (b) whether the proceeds of
the cess levied under the Punjab Social Security Act, 2000
could be credited directly to the Punjab Social Security
Fund without first forming part of the Consolidated Fund
of the State under Article 266 of the Constitution, are
left open. Nothing stated in this order shall be construed
as an expression of opinion on these questions;
iii. All other contentions of the parties in the individual
matters, including those relating to the assessments, the

--- Page 358 ---
4
periods of levy, and the consequential reliefs, are also
left open;
iv. The Registry is directed to list the lead matter, and the
connected matters before the appropriate regular Bench(es)
for disposal on their individual merits, in accordance
with the observations made hereinabove and after taking
requisite directions from the Chief Justice of India on
the administrative side.
In  answer  to  the  reference,  Hon’ble  Mr.  Justice  K.V.
Viswanathan  pronounced  a  separate  judgment  directing  as
follows: 
1. Let the appeals arising out of challenge to the provisions
under  the  Orissa  Sales  Tax  Act,  1947  (Civil  Appeal  No
8763/1994 and Civil Appeal No 8909/1994) and the Punjab
General Sales Tax Act, 1948 (Civil Appeal No 98/2003, Civil
Appeal Nos. 831-850/2003, Civil Appeal No 851/2003, Civil
Appeal No 99/2003 and Civil Appeal No 100/2003) be placed
before  the  Hon’ble  Chief  Justice  for  assignment  to  an
appropriate Bench to be decided in accordance with law as laid
down in S. Kodar (supra).  
2. Let the appeals concerning the validity of the levy under the
Punjab Social Security Act, 2000 (Civil Appeal No 7485/2001,
Civil Appeal arising out of SLP (C) Nos 22159-22180/2002,
Civil Appeal No 5046/2003 and Civil Appeal No 5637/2008) be

Date : 06-11-2026 This matter was called on for hearing today.
CORAM : 
         HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE J.B. PARDIWALA
         HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE MANMOHAN 
For Petitioner(s) : 
                   Mr. Shyam Divan, Sr. Adv.

                   Ms. Mani Munjal, Adv.
                   Mr. Parth Yadav- 4035, AOR                   
For Respondent(s) : 
          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
1. The  petitioner  before  us  came  to  be  arrested  by  the
Respondent No.3 under Section 104 of the Customs Act, 1962, (for
short, 'the Act 1962'). 
2. The Respondent No.2 before us is the DRI, and the Respondent
No. 3 before us is the Officer of its Indore Zonal Unit.
3. It is the Respondent No.3 who arrested the petitioner and is
conducting the investigation. 
4. The petitioner has invoked the writ jurisdiction of this Court
under  Article  32  of  the  Constitution  and  has  prayed for the

--- Page 360 ---
2
following reliefs: 
“a. issue a writ order or direction in the nature of mandamus
directing the respondents to release the petitioner in C. Case
No. 91 of 2026 pending before the Ld. Additional Chief Judicial
Magistrate, Bongaon, North 24 Parganas, arising out of F. No.
DRI/IZU/96-2026/CI/INT-70/ENQ-26 of the Directorate of Revenue
Intelligence, concerning the alleged offences under Sections
132,  135(l)(a)  and  135(l)(b)  of  the  Customs  Act,  1962,
punishable under Section 135(l)(i)(A) and (B) of the said Act,
on such terms and conditions as this Hon'ble Court may deem fit
and proper;
b. declare that the arrest of the Petitioner on 06.10.2026 under
Section 104 of the Customs Act, 1962 and his continued detention
are in violation Section 187(3) BNSS and Articles 14, 21 and 22
of the Constitution of India and the law laid down by this
Hon'ble Court in the case of Radhika Agarwal V. Union of India,
(2025) 6 SCC 545;
c. direct the Respondent Nos. 2 and 3 to place on record before
this Hon'ble Court the "reasons to believe" recorded under
Section 104(1) of the Customs Act, 1962 at the time of the
Petitioner's  arrest,  and  the  material  on  which  they  were
founded;
d. pass such other or further order(s) as this Hon'ble Court may
deem fit and proper in the facts and circumstances of the case.”
5. According to the petitioner, the following questions of law
fall for the consideration of this Court:- 
“A. Whether the arrest of the Petitioner under Section 104(1) of
the Customs Act, 1962, solely on the basis of the statement of a
co-accused under Section 108 and after a search that yielded
nothing, satisfies the requirement of "reasons to believe"
founded on material as laid down in Radhika Agarwal v. Union of
India, (2025) 6 SCC 545?
B. Whether the Respondents were bound to record and furnish to
the Petitioner, and place before the remanding Magistrate, the
written "reasons to believe" under Section 104(1), and whether
failure to do so vitiates the arrest and the consequent remand?
C. Whether the denial of access to counsel during interrogation
and DRI custody violates Article 22(1) of the Constitution and
Section 38 of the BNSS, and vitiates the continued custody of
the Petitioner?
D. Whether keeping the Petitioner in the control of DRI officers
for about 23 hours, through the night, before formally recording
his arrest violates Articles 21 and 22 of the Constitution?
E. Whether remand orders passed without recording satisfaction
as to the lawfulness of the arrest and the existence of adequate
grounds  under  Section  187(3)  of  the  BNSS  are  without
jurisdiction?

--- Page 361 ---
3
F.  Whether  the  statement  of  a  co-accused,  which  is  not
substantive  evidence,  can  by  itself  justify  the  continued
detention of an accused?
G. Whether the continued detention of the Petitioner, when every
other co-accused including the alleged "mastermind" and the
maker of the statement implicating him has been released,
violates Articles 14 and 21 of the Constitution?
6. We heard Mr. Shyam Divan and Mr. P.B. Suresh, the learned
Senior Counsel appearing for the petitioner.
7. We enquired with Mr. Divan as to why the petitioner has
thought fit to invoke the writ jurisdiction of this Court under
Article 32 of the Constitution, more particularly when the very
same reliefs could have been looked into by the High Court in
exercise  of  its  writ  jurisdiction  under  Article  226  of  the
Constitution. 
8. Be that as it may, we take notice of the fact that the
petitioner prayed for bail before the Chief Judicial Magistrate.
9. The Chief Judicial Magistrate, vide Order dated 27th October,
2026, rejected the bail application. 
10. We are informed that thereafter the petitioner went before the
Sessions Court and prayed for bail.
11. However,  since  the  Respondents  prayed  for  time  to  file
counter, and a long date was given by the Sessions Court, the
petitioner thought fit not to press the bail application and
withdrew the same. 
12. We believe that the first step at the end of the petitioner
should have been to get himself released on bail.
13. In such circumstances, we permit the petitioner to go before
the High Court of Calcutta and pray for bail at the earliest.
14. Insofar as the other reliefs are concerned, the petitioner
shall prefer a Writ Petition under Article 226 of the Constitution.
15. If any bail application is preferred, the High Court shall
look into the same expeditiously in accordance with law.

--- Page 362 ---
4
16. With the aforesaid, this petition stands disposed of.
17. Pending applications, if any, also stand disposed of.
 (VISHAL ANAND)                                    (POOJA SHARMA)

S.L.P. (Crl.) No.9591/2026:
3. We  have  heard  Mr.  Ravi  Prakash  Mehrotra,  learned  senior  counsel

4. In course arguing the claims raised in both the petitions, Mr. Mehrotra
submits that the petitioner has two properties in the State of Uttar Pradesh and

5. According to Mr. Mehrotra, the value of such properties is much more than

of Judicature at Allahabad, i.e., Rs.2,29,34,161/- (Rupees two crore twenty-nine
lakh thirty-four thousand one hundred and sixty-one) only. 
6. We  require  the  petitioner  to  file  an affidavit by  16th November,  2026
pleading that the three properties, particulars whereof are to be mentioned in
such affidavit in clear terms, are unencumbered and can be put up for sale
without any hindrance.

2

--- Page 486 ---

       UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                          O R D E R
1. Having considered the submissions made by the counsel for the
parties, what transpires is that in pursuance to a representation
which was submitted by the petitioner to the State authorities, the
said representation was forwarded to respondent no. 2.  The said
respondent, on consideration, replied to the Competent Authority in
the State along with the details therein with regard to the claim
of the petitioner.  It was left open to the State to take a final
call on the same.
2. Learned counsel for the State has informed the Court that
after the consideration of the response of respondent no. 2, a
communication has been sent to the said respondent for taking a
final decision thereon.
 
3. Learned counsel for respondent no. 2, when called upon to
indicate as to what decision has been taken thereon submits that
final decision will be taken within a period of six weeks from
today and the decision so taken communicated to the petitioner
within a period of further two weeks.
4. It goes without saying that in case, the claim of the
petitioner is accepted, the consequential steps be taken for giving
effect thereto.  In case, it goes otherwise, it would be open to
the petitioner to avail of their remedies as may be available in
accordance with law.
5. It may be observed that the impugned order dated 24.06.2026
passed by the High Court shall not in itself be an impediment for
the petitioner to avail of their abovesaid remedy.
6. The Special Leave Petition is disposed of.
7. Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed of.

2
3. By virtue of her admission and due to continuation of the writ
proceedings, the respondent has completed around three and a half

          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
The petitioner-husband has approached this Court challenging
the order dated 04.05.2026 passed by the High Court of Orissa at
Cuttack in RPFAM No. 95 of 2025, where by the High Court reduced
the maintenance awarded to the respondent-wife from Rs.10,000/-
(Rupees Ten Thousand Only) to Rs. 8,000/- (Rupees Eight Thousand
Only) per month.
The Court is apprised that arrears of maintenance amounting to
approximately Rs.4,00,000/-(Rupees Four Lakhs Only) are outstanding

--- Page 1012 ---
2
against the petitioner-Husband.
An  inquiry  was  made  from  the  learned  counsel  for  the
petitioner as to whether the petitioner-husband is ready to clear
at least a part of the aforesaid arrears. However, learned counsel
submits that he has no instructions in this regard.
We have heard the arguments advanced by the learned counsel
for the petitioner on merits.
We find no reason to interfere in the impugned order passed by
the High Court granting maintenance at the rate of Rs.8,000/-
(Rupees Eight Thousand Only) per month to the respondent-wife.
The respondent-Wife would be at liberty to approach the Family
Court for recovery of the outstanding arrears.
The Family Court shall take appropriate measures (if necessary
coercive steps) to ensure that the arrears of maintenance, as well
as  the  regular  monthly  maintenance,  are  recovered  from  the
petitioner-husband and paid to the respondent-wife. 
In view of the above, the Special Leave Petition stands
dismissed, as being devoid of merit.
Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed of.

2. Though the petitioner’s application for suspension of
sentence is pending before the High Court, we have been informed
that  his  mother  is  presently  hospitalized  and  on  ventilator
support. We have also been informed that she may not survive till
the next date of hearing fixed by the High Court. In these
circumstances, we dispose of this Special Leave Petition with the
direction that, in the event of the unfortunate demise of the
petitioner’s mother, the petitioner shall be released on interim
bail for a period of two days, subject to such terms and conditions
as the Trial Court may deem fit to impose. Ordered accordingly.
3. As a result, the pending interlocutory applications, if
any, also stand disposed of.

We have heard learned counsel for the respective parties
and perused the material on record.
The High Court has rightly noted that on the lapse of
period   of   two years,  the  matter  has been rendered academic. 
contd..

--- Page 1214 ---
- 2 -
However, the direction has been issued to constitute Non-Hereditary
Trust  Board  under  Section  27  of  the  Odisha  Hindu  Religious
Endowments Act, 1951.
Learned  counsel  for  the  petitioners  submitted  that  the
petitioners are Hereditary Trustees and they have a right to be
considered for the purpose of appointment as Hereditary Trustees.  
In  the  circumstances,  we  direct  the  learned  Additional
Assistant Commissioner of Endowments, Cuttack to consider the
matter afresh under Section 27 of the aforesaid Act after giving an
opportunity of hearing to the petitioners herein, who may ventilate
their grievance before the said authority.
On hearing the petitioners and all concerned, the Additional
Assistant Commissioner of Endowments, Cuttack shall pass a speaking
order.
All contentions on both sides are left open to be advanced
before the competent authority.  
The Special Leave Petition is disposed of in the aforesaid
terms.
Pending application(s) shall stand disposed of.
